cards.title: Lightest Spark
cards.flavor: The most common element in the universe. One proton, one electron, endless fuel for stars.

cards.title: Sun Gas
cards.flavor: Named for helios, Greek for sun. It was spotted in sunlight before anyone found it on Earth.

cards.title: Battery Blood
cards.flavor: Soft enough to cut with a knife. Rechargeable batteries love it.

cards.title: Space Mirror
cards.flavor: Light yet stiff. The James Webb Space Telescope's mirrors are made of it.

cards.title: Green Flame
cards.flavor: Boron compounds burn green in a flame. Add it to glass and you get heat-proof borosilicate.

cards.title: Diamond Maker
cards.flavor: Graphite in your pencil, diamond in a ring. Same atom, wildly different moods.

cards.title: Air Boss
cards.flavor: Fills about 78% of the air around you. Plenty of room to orbit.

cards.title: Breath of Life
cards.flavor: About 21% of the air is oxygen. Take a deep breath, then keep climbing.

cards.title: Electron Grabber
cards.flavor: Fluorine is the most electronegative element. It snatches electrons like nothing else.

cards.title: Neon Glow
cards.flavor: Zap neon gas with electricity and it glows red-orange. Hello, city lights.

cards.title: Splash Danger
cards.flavor: Drop it in water and it fizzes wildly. Pair it with chlorine and you get table salt.

cards.title: Blinding Burner
cards.flavor: Burns with a dazzling white light. Old camera flashes used it.

cards.title: Light Metal
cards.flavor: Light, tough and endlessly recyclable. Your soda can approves.

cards.title: Chip Maker
cards.flavor: Silicon is the heart of computer chips. Your phone is full of it.

cards.title: Light Bearer
cards.flavor: Found in 1669 by boiling down urine. Its name means 'light-bearer.'

cards.title: Volcano Yellow
cards.flavor: Bright yellow crystals near volcanoes. Matches and gunpowder both use it.

cards.title: Pool Party
cards.flavor: Keeps swimming pools clean. Bonded to sodium, it seasons your fries.

cards.title: The Lazy One
cards.flavor: Its name means 'lazy' in Greek, because it barely reacts with anything.

cards.title: Banana Power
cards.flavor: Bananas are famous for it. Its symbol K comes from kalium.

cards.title: Bone Builder
cards.flavor: Builds your bones and teeth. Chalk and limestone are packed with it.

cards.title: Nordic Namesake
cards.flavor: Named after Scandinavia. A pinch strengthens aluminium bike frames and bats.

cards.title: Titan Tough
cards.flavor: As strong as steel but far lighter. Named for the Titans of Greek myth.

cards.title: Tool Steel Booster
cards.flavor: Named for Vanadis, a Norse goddess. A dash of it toughens steel tools.

cards.title: Mirror Shine
cards.flavor: Its name means 'color' in Greek. It gives chrome that mirror shine.

cards.title: Steel's Sidekick
cards.flavor: Steel needs it to be tough. Your body needs a trace too.

cards.title: Core Metal
cards.flavor: Iron fills Earth's core, and your red blood cells use it to carry oxygen.

cards.title: Deep Blue
cards.flavor: Cobalt blue has tinted glass and pottery for centuries. It's also in batteries.

cards.title: Pocket Change
cards.flavor: It's in your coins. The US five-cent piece is even named after it.

cards.title: Wire Runner
cards.flavor: Carries electricity through wires. Left in the air, it turns green, like the Statue of Liberty.

cards.title: Rust Shield
cards.flavor: Zinc coats steel to fight rust. That's called galvanizing.

cards.title: Melts in Hand
cards.flavor: Melts at about 30°C. Hold it in your hand and watch it turn liquid.

cards.title: Transistor Pioneer
cards.flavor: Built the first transistors. Named for Germany by Clemens Winkler.

cards.title: Poison Classic
cards.flavor: A notorious poison. Handle with care, and keep your shells tight.

cards.title: Moon Element
cards.flavor: Named for Selene, the Greek moon goddess. Its electrical resistance changes with light.

cards.title: Stinky Liquid
cards.flavor: One of only two elements liquid at room temperature. Its name means 'stench.'

cards.title: The Hidden One
cards.flavor: Its name means 'hidden' in Greek. Found in 1898 by chilling air until it turned liquid.

cards.title: Ruby Lines
cards.flavor: Named from Latin for deep red, the color of its spectral lines.

cards.title: Crimson Fireworks
cards.flavor: Burns bright red. Fireworks and flares use it for crimson.

cards.title: Ytterby's Gift
cards.flavor: Named for Ytterby, a Swedish village. Four elements got their names from it.

cards.title: Diamond Double
cards.flavor: Cubic zirconia, a diamond lookalike, is made from its oxide.

cards.title: Niobe's Metal
cards.flavor: Named for Niobe of Greek myth. It strengthens steel and MRI magnets.

cards.title: Heat Survivor
cards.flavor: Helps steel survive blazing heat. Its name comes from the Greek word for lead.

cards.title: Human-Made First
cards.flavor: The first element made by humans. Doctors use it in medical scans.

cards.title: Russian Roots
cards.flavor: Named for Ruthenia, Latin for Russia. Tiny amounts harden platinum.

cards.title: Rose Rarity
cards.flavor: Its name means 'rose.' Super pricey and found in car catalytic converters.

cards.title: Asteroid Namesake
cards.flavor: Named after the asteroid Pallas. Palladium cleans car exhaust.

cards.title: Top Conductor
cards.flavor: Silver conducts electricity better than any other metal. Its symbol Ag is from argentum.

cards.title: Battery Veteran
cards.flavor: Once powered rechargeable NiCd batteries. It's toxic, so its use is fading.

cards.title: Indigo Line
cards.flavor: Named for the indigo line in its spectrum. Touchscreens use it.

cards.title: Bronze Age Buddy
cards.flavor: Alloyed with copper, it made bronze thousands of years ago.

cards.title: Ancient Makeup
cards.flavor: Ancient eye makeup used its compounds. Symbol Sb comes from Latin stibium.

cards.title: Earth Element
cards.flavor: Named for Tellus, Latin for Earth. Rare, but used in solar panels.

cards.title: Purple Vapor
cards.flavor: Its vapor is violet. Your thyroid needs it to work.

cards.title: The Stranger
cards.flavor: Its name means 'stranger' in Greek. Bright headlights and ion thrusters use it.

cards.title: Clock Keeper
cards.flavor: Caesium atoms run the atomic clocks that define the second. Blink and they've ticked billions of times.

cards.title: Heavy Hitter
cards.flavor: Its name means 'heavy.' Doctors use a barium drink to light up X-rays.

cards.title: Row Leader
cards.flavor: Its name means 'to lie hidden.' It leads a whole row of elements.

cards.title: Spark Maker
cards.flavor: Cerium sparks lighter flints. Named for the dwarf planet Ceres.

cards.title: Green Twin
cards.flavor: Its name means 'green twin.' It tints glass a yellow-green.

cards.title: Magnet Master
cards.flavor: Makes super-strong magnets for headphones and electric motors.

cards.title: Titan's Fire
cards.flavor: Named for Prometheus, the Titan who stole fire. It's radioactive.

cards.title: Mineral Namesake
cards.flavor: Named for the mineral samarskite. Samarium-cobalt magnets shrug off heat.

cards.title: Euro Glow
cards.flavor: Named for Europe. Euro banknotes use it for glowing security ink.

cards.title: MRI Helper
cards.flavor: Named for chemist Johan Gadolin. It makes MRI scans clearer.

cards.title: Green Screen Glow
cards.flavor: Named for Ytterby. It gives some screens a green glow.

cards.title: Hard to Get
cards.flavor: Its name means 'hard to get' in Greek. Its magnets keep working even when hot.

cards.title: Stockholm Strength
cards.flavor: Named for Holmia, Latin for Stockholm. No element has a stronger magnetic moment.

cards.title: Pink Fiber Boost
cards.flavor: Named for Ytterby. It boosts light signals in fiber-optic cables and tints glass pink.

cards.title: Thule Rarity
cards.flavor: Named for Thule, an old name for Scandinavia. One of the rarest of the rare earths.

cards.title: Ytterby Again
cards.flavor: The fourth element named for Ytterby. Its atoms tick inside super-precise clocks.

cards.title: Paris Metal
cards.flavor: Named for Lutetia, the Roman name for Paris. It closes out the lanthanide row.

cards.title: Copenhagen Metal
cards.flavor: Named for Hafnia, Latin for Copenhagen. Nuclear reactor control rods use it.

cards.title: Phone Capacitor
cards.flavor: Named for Tantalus of Greek myth. Tiny capacitors in phones are made with it.

cards.title: Melt-Proof
cards.flavor: Melts at about 3,400°C, the highest of any metal. Its symbol W comes from wolfram.

cards.title: Rhine's Last Find
cards.flavor: Named for the Rhine. It was the last stable element found in nature.

cards.title: Dense Champ
cards.flavor: Osmium is the densest natural element. Its name comes from the Greek for 'smell.'

cards.title: Rainbow Messenger
cards.flavor: A thin iridium layer in rock marks the asteroid impact that ended the dinosaurs.

cards.title: Little Silver
cards.flavor: Its name means 'little silver' in Spanish. Catalytic converters use it.

cards.title: Golden Goal
cards.flavor: Gold can be hammered into sheets thin enough to see through. Symbol Au is from aurum.

cards.title: Liquid Silver
cards.flavor: Liquid at room temperature. Named for the planet Mercury; its symbol Hg means 'liquid silver.'

cards.title: Green Shoot
cards.flavor: Named from the Greek for 'green shoot,' after its bright green spectral line.

cards.title: Plumbing Pioneer
cards.flavor: Romans piped water through it. Plumbing gets its name from plumbum, Latin for lead.

cards.title: Rainbow Crystal
cards.flavor: Grown bismuth crystals form shimmering rainbow staircases. Pepto-Bismol uses it.

cards.title: Poland's Pride
cards.flavor: Marie Curie named it for her homeland, Poland. It's intensely radioactive.

cards.title: Unstable One
cards.flavor: Its name means 'unstable.' It's the rarest element found naturally on Earth.

cards.title: Basement Gas
cards.flavor: A radioactive gas that seeps up from the ground. Homes can be tested for it.

cards.title: Fleeting France
cards.flavor: Named for France by Marguerite Perey. It lasts only minutes before decaying.

cards.title: Ray of Light
cards.flavor: Found by Marie and Pierre Curie. Its name means 'ray,' and old watch dials used it to glow.

cards.title: Blue Glow
cards.flavor: Its name means 'ray' in Greek. It glows pale blue in the dark.

cards.title: Thunder Metal
cards.flavor: Named for Thor, Norse god of thunder. It's a possible future nuclear fuel.

cards.title: Before Actinium
cards.flavor: Its name means 'before actinium,' because it decays into actinium.

cards.title: Power Plant Fuel
cards.flavor: Named for the planet Uranus. It fuels nuclear power plants.

cards.title: Beyond Uranium
cards.flavor: The first element past uranium on the table. Named for Neptune.

cards.title: Probe Power
cards.flavor: Named for Pluto. A plutonium isotope powers deep-space probes like Voyager.

cards.title: Smoke Alarm Atom
cards.flavor: Named for the Americas. Many smoke detectors use a speck of it.

cards.title: Curie Tribute
cards.flavor: Marie and Pierre Curie pioneered radioactivity. This element carries their name.

cards.title: Berkeley Born
cards.flavor: First made in 1949 at Berkeley, California. The city is right there in its name.

cards.title: Neutron Source
cards.flavor: Named for California. A tiny pinch makes a powerful source of neutrons.

cards.title: Einstein's Element
cards.flavor: First found in debris from a 1952 nuclear test. Its name honors Albert Einstein.

cards.title: Fermi's Element
cards.flavor: Turned up in the same 1952 test debris as einsteinium. It honors Enrico Fermi.

cards.title: Table Architect
cards.flavor: Mendeleev built the periodic table. You're climbing it.

cards.title: Prize Namesake
cards.flavor: Named for Alfred Nobel, the founder of the Nobel Prizes.

cards.title: Cyclotron Honor
cards.flavor: Named for Ernest Lawrence, who invented the cyclotron particle accelerator.

cards.title: Nucleus Finder
cards.flavor: Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus. Your core owes him one.

cards.title: Dubna Debut
cards.flavor: Named for Dubna, the Russian town whose lab helped discover it.

cards.title: Living Legend
cards.flavor: Seaborg got his own element while he was still alive. Rare honor.

cards.title: Model Maker
cards.flavor: Niels Bohr's atom model inspired this very game. This element honors him.

cards.title: Hesse Heavyweight
cards.flavor: Named for Hesse, the German state where it was first made.

cards.title: Fission Pioneer
cards.flavor: Lise Meitner helped explain nuclear fission. Meitnerium is her tribute.

cards.title: Darmstadt Debut
cards.flavor: Named for Darmstadt, Germany, where it was first made.

cards.title: X-Ray Honor
cards.flavor: Röntgen found X-rays. Now he's on the table too.

cards.title: Sun Centered
cards.flavor: Named for Nicolaus Copernicus, who put the Sun at the center of the solar system.

cards.title: Rising Sun
cards.flavor: Discovered in Japan and named for Nihon. It's the first element named in Asia.

cards.title: Flerov's Lab
cards.flavor: Made at the Flerov Laboratory in Russia, which gave it its name.

cards.title: Moscow Made
cards.flavor: Made at a lab in the Moscow region. The region gave it its name.

cards.title: Livermore Lab
cards.flavor: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California helped make it, and lent its name.

cards.title: Tennessee Teamwork
cards.flavor: Tennessee labs helped make it possible, so the state got the name.

cards.title: Table Topper
cards.flavor: Named for physicist Yuri Oganessian. The heaviest element on the table. Reach it and you win.
